content:
maria chen: Quick follow-up to the console query authz RFC — I sketched a small alternative where we insert an authz-aware projection cache between the query gateway and the projection service. Wanted to get reactions before I turn it into a short RFC.

kevin r: sketch pls. what problem are we trying to avoid that the current pushdown approach doesn’t handle?

sasha li: mainly the cold-path amplification + cross-tenant permission checks causing high p95. if we can cache per-token/per-principal projections we avoid re-eval + costly joins.

maria chen: exactly. current plan (pushdown) means every tile request hits the projection service and authz engine. spikes on tenant lookups blow up latency. idea: a lightweight projection cache that stores small projection blobs guarded by an authz key (derived from caller and route). cache is strongly typed and limited to short TTLs (30–120s).

kevin r: concern: explosion of cache cardinality + correctness for rollouts (canary models that change shape). how do we invalidate when projection schema changes or when a canary is rolled out?

maria chen: two parts: 1) key includes projection-version and model-spec fingerprint. 2) we keep a simple invalidation channel — when we deploy a new projection version we broadcast invalidation to the cache tier; the cache client can also fall back to bypass on schema mismatch.

daniel (dan): can you show a representative key format?

maria chen: sure - example pseudoconfig: 
```
cache_key = tenant_id + ':' + projection_name + ':' + projection_version + ':' + principal_hash
ttl = 45s
mode = per-tenant (optional global hotset)
```

sasha li: perf numbers? hit-rate assumptions?

maria chen: prototype on local replay (dashboard query mix) gave ~55% hit rate at ttl=45s with realistic user flows; p95 token latency for the gateway dropped ~18% under load. very preliminary.

kevin r: 55% is promising. What about RBAC semantics — we must guarantee we never leak data across principals. Using principal_hash is fine but careful with shared-group permissions (e.g., team-level grants).

maria chen: agreed. the key derivation can include an ordered list of authorization attributes (groups, roles) hashed in a canonical way. If the attribute set grows too large we fall back to no-cache for that request.

daniel (dan): how would this interact with our current token sampling telemetry and billing? caching changes token counts and could mask regression signals.

maria chen: good call. plan: augment telemetry to surface cached vs uncached token counts per route/model. billing will still count gateway-level tokens; we’ll add a reconciliation job to ensure transparency. Also add a "cache_only" flag for experiments so we can measure user-visible diffs.

sasha li: rollout strategy? prefer server-side flag first or config-driven on the gateway?

maria chen: gateway-side feature flag so we can gate by tenant and by route. start with internal tenants + a couple of friendly customers. if stable, flip on more broadly and enable auto-eviction thresholds.

kevin r: operationally: where do we host this cache? in-process on the projection instances or as a separate fleet?

maria chen: separate fleet (small memcached-like nodes) to avoid adding jitter to projection cpu. plus separate autoscaling gives us better control. we keep a small in-process LRU as a hot-layer to reduce network hops.

daniel (dan): failure mode: cache partition loss — must ensure graceful degradation to pushdown without SLA surprise. Also need to ensure we don't silently degrade correctness when broadcasting invalidations misses.

maria chen: agreed — fallback semantics: if cache is unreachable or invalidation lag detected, gateway falls back to direct pushdown to projection service. We also emit an alert when cache-miss ratio or fallback rate exceeds thresholds.

sasha li: any changes required in the projection service API?

maria chen: small addition: projection service should be able to serve a "projection fingerprint" endpoint and a schema version header on responses. That allows cache keying and detect mismatches. Backwards compatible.

kevin r: sounds reasonable. Can you capture the tradeoffs in the RFC? I want a section on: cardinality vs latency, correctness guarantees, operational surface, telemetry changes, and rollout plan.

maria chen: will do. Drafting now — will post a short RFC PR tomorrow. Thanks for the quick checks — any other blockers?

daniel (dan): add a short experiment plan: sample 1% traffic -> measure p95, token counts, authz error rate, cache-induced 403s (should be zero).

sasha li: and add a teardown checklist for invalidation bugs.

deploy-bot: @maria chen created a draft RFC: https://redwood/infra/rfcs/console-projection-cache-draft (internal) :eyes:

maria chen: linking the draft here. will iterate with the notes above and ping infra and security for a quick review. :thumbsup:
